title: Spiced Poached Pears
subtitle: Pears poached in a spiced honey syrup
excerpt: Whole pears poached in a fragrant syrup of honey, orange, star anise, and warm spices. They look elegant and are almost completely hands-off to make.
sourceNotes: Inspired by classic French poires pochees au vin and adapted to use a spiced honey syrup rather than wine.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Poach up to 2 days ahead and keep the pears in the syrup in the fridge. The flavour deepens with time.

content.text: Choose pears that are ripe but still firm. Very ripe pears will turn mushy during poaching.
Put the red wine vinegar, honey, orange juice and zest, and 300ml of water in a large saucepan.
Add the star anise, cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Stir to dissolve the honey. Lower the peeled pears into the syrup.
Cut a circle of baking paper to fit inside the pan and place it on top of the pears. This keeps them submerged.
Poach at a gentle simmer for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Remove the pears and set aside. Boil the syrup for 5 minutes to reduce and thicken slightly.
Serve the pears warm or at room temperature with the syrup spooned over.

items.symptom: Pears are still firm after 25 minutes.
items.cause: Pears were too firm or heat too low.
items.fix: Continue poaching for a further 10 minutes and check again.

items.symptom: Pears have turned mushy and falling apart.
items.cause: Overripe fruit or poached too long.
items.fix: Use firm pears and check with a knife at 20 minutes.

items.cause: Red wine vinegar is quite acidic.
items.fix: Stir in a little more honey to balance the sharpness.
